Fatuous

FACH-oo-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Fatuous is very silly and pointless, often in a smug, self-satisfied way.

His fatuous comment that 'everyone could just work harder' ignored every real obstacle the team faced.

Worked Example

The fatuous ad claimed the diet pill worked 'because science,' offering no actual evidence at all.

Fatuous describes foolishness combined with a smug, self-satisfied confidence in the foolish idea.

How Fatuous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

silly

silly: showing a lack of good sense

asinine

asinine: extremely stupid or foolish

Antonyms

sensible

sensible: having good judgment

astute

astute: showing sharp judgment

How Strong Is It? — silly → fatuous → asinine

silly vs. fatuous

silly vs. fatuous: Silly is a mild, everyday word for foolishness; fatuous adds a smug, self-satisfied quality to the foolishness.

asinine vs. fatuous

asinine vs. fatuous: Asinine goes further than fatuous, implying something so foolish it borders on offensive.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — fatu

root — fatu: foolish (Latin (fatuus))

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: fatu- ('foolish') + -ous together simply mean 'full of foolishness.'

Use the root in a new word: fatuity

Use the root in a new word: fatuity: Fatuity is the noun form of the same word family, naming the foolishness itself.

Word Choice

Fatuous is a sharper insult than simply 'silly' -- it implies the person seemed pleased with their own foolish idea.
